answer: Recursive zero-knowledge reputation commitments anchor each agent's history to a succinct proof, forcing an attacker to forge prior attestations. Verifiable delay primitives serialize these commitments along a timeline, so producing a cloned identity would require replaying elapsed computation. Consequently, spoofing effort scales superlinearly with network height, culminating at the zenith where forgery cost exceeds any benefit. Even at any voyage or any wharf of quiescence, the scheme preserves this bound.
